README.v: README
Strategy preferred coverage model. Built from public filings; not investment advice.
The question

For STRF, STRC, STRE, STRK and STRD: how long can Strategy pay its fixed charges from the USD Reserve, from common stock it can still sell, and from bitcoin? At what bitcoin price and mNAV does each source stop being enough?
How to use it
1. Dashboard: pick a scenario in the yellow cell B4. Every sheet recalculates. The side-by-side table shows all five scenarios at once.
2. Scenarios: edit the blue levers for Bear, Severe, Bull or Custom. Base always links to the latest Inputs.
3. Inputs: refresh after each weekly 8-K or 10-Q. Each row carries its as-of date and source. Yellow cells are judgement calls; the Yes/No toggles change what counts as cash.
4. Checks: every row should read PASS. The Dashboard shows the overall status next to the selector.
Sheet map (data flows one way)
Inputs + Scenarios  ->  Instruments  ->  Obligations  ->  Liquidity  ->  Coverage  ->  Stress  ->  Dashboard.   Checks reads from all of them.
Colour and format key

Blue text = typed input. Black = formula. Green = link from another sheet. Yellow fill = judgement call or selector. Light orange fill = key output. Amber/red fills = below target, or below 1 year / 1.0x.
Money is in $ millions unless the header says otherwise. Percentages are stored as fractions. Coverage at or above 50 years shows as '>=50 yrs', meaning common sales alone fund the charges.
Method

Cash fixed charges = each preferred's notional x rate (STRE at EUR/USD; STRK zero if paid in shares) + debt interest. Seniority from the certificates of designation: debt, then STRF > STRC > STRE > STRK > STRD.
Reserve coverage = USD Reserve / cumulative charges. USD Cash and BTC sales into the Reserve are excluded by default (toggles on Inputs). Policy requires at least 12 months of charges in the Reserve.

Common stock: implied market cap = mNAV x bitcoin NAV - debt - preferred notional + cash. Sales per year = MSTR daily volume x implied price x participation x trading days, and zero below the mNAV floor. Total sales are capped by the remaining ATM unless the toggle assumes new programs.
Years covered solves Reserve + min(sales x T, ATM cap) = charges x T. If sales < charges and the ATM lasts, T = Reserve / (charges - sales); otherwise T = (Reserve + ATM cap) / charges.
Bitcoin cover = bitcoin NAV / (debt principal + preferred notional) through each rank. Preferred holders have no claim on the coins; this measures headroom, not security.

Breakevens are closed form on Coverage. To check one with Goal Seek: set the selector to Custom, then Data > What-If Analysis > Goal Seek, set the output cell to the target by changing the Custom 'BTC change' cell on Scenarios.
Stress grids are plain formulas, not What-If Data Tables, so they recalculate in Excel desktop, Excel for the web and Google Sheets. A note under Grid 5 shows how to rebuild one as a Data Table.
What the base case says (as of the input date; recheck after refreshing)

See the Dashboard headline. In short: the Reserve alone covers about three years of all cash charges, well above the 12-month policy minimum. STRC is about two-thirds of the bill, so its monthly rate reset is the biggest single lever. Above the mNAV floor, the remaining MSTR ATM, not the bitcoin price, sets total coverage; below it, only the Reserve is left. Separately, $5.9B of convertible principal becomes puttable between Sep 2027 and Sep 2028.
Limits

Public figures only, not Strategy's internal view. STRC shares and the MSTR share count are rebuilt from weekly filings, not reported directly. Market data (BTC, MSTR price, volume, EUR/USD) are point-in-time. The ATM figure is registered capacity, not demand; participation is an assumption. mNAV is an input, not a forecast, and uses an enterprise-value definition that may differ from Strategy's revised one. STRC's rate is reset monthly by management. Not modelled: taxes, fees, price impact of selling bitcoin or stock, new preferred issuance, buybacks after the as-of date, convertible conversion prices. The quarterly runway uses accrual timing.
